data.name: Ruin
data.detailed_description:
Welcome to Ruin, a medieval fantasy sandbox MMORPG where players build homes, form guilds, explore an open world, master professions, conquer dungeons, and fight for territory.

Ruin is inspired by the slower, social feel of classic MMORPGs while giving players greater freedom to shape the world around them. Explore alone or with others, gather resources, craft equipment, build settlements, discover dangerous places and develop your character through the activities you choose.

A Medieval Sandbox MMORPG

Ruin is an open world MMORPG built around exploration, progression and player freedom.

Choose a class, learn new abilities, discover runes that change how you play, collect equipment and develop your character while exploring a persistent medieval fantasy world.

Whether you prefer questing, crafting, building, PvP, dungeons, gathering or simply exploring, there are different ways to progress.

Build a Home and Shape the World

Build and maintain your house, place furniture and crafting stations, store resources and develop the surrounding land through terraforming.

Players can gather materials throughout the world and use them to expand what they have built rather than simply returning to a static town between adventures.

Guilds can take this further by establishing their own territory and constructing shared settlements.

Form Guilds and Build Settlements

Guilds can claim territory, terraform the land, construct defensive walls and gates, place shared buildings and manage permissions for their settlement.

Expanding a guild town creates a larger space for members to build, craft, gather and prepare for adventures together.

Explore a Living Fantasy World

Travel through forests, settlements, coastlines, islands, caves and dangerous regions filled with creatures, resources and hidden locations.

The world features changing weather, rain, fog, wind and a day-and-night cycle that alter the atmosphere as you travel.

Bring a cart for supplies, sail the ocean to new lands, go fishing, search for resources or simply head away from established roads and see what you find.

Dungeons and Group Challenges

Tank, healer and damage roles each have an important part to play as your group fights through enemies and bosses in search of better equipment and valuable rewards.

At higher levels, players can take on more difficult Heroic and Heroic+ challenges with increasingly dangerous encounters and improved rewards.

Fight Other Players

Fight other players in organized battlegrounds or encounter conflict while exploring contested areas of the open world.

Guild settlements can be fortified with walls, gates and defensive structures, giving player built locations a meaningful place within the world.

Choose a Class and Shape Your Build

Each class has its own abilities and playstyle, using runes provide additional ways to modify abilities and develop different builds.

Collect equipment, improve your character and experiment with combinations that suit the way you want to play.

Craft, Gather and Trade

Professions are an important part of the world.

Gather resources and use them for crafting, construction and trade. Players can fish, cook, farm, gather materials and create useful equipment and supplies.

Items can be traded between players through the economy, allowing dedicated gatherers and crafters to have a place alongside adventurers and combat-focused players.

Your Place in Ruin

There is no single path through the game.

Build a home. Create a guild town. Master a profession. Explore the wilderness. Hunt for rare equipment. Complete difficult dungeons. Fight other players. Trade with the community.

Ruin is an independently developed MMORPG focused on creating a world where progression is not only about increasing your level, but also about what you build, discover and leave behind.

reviews.review:
Ruin is an ambitious fantasy sandbox MMORPG that attempts to capture the freedom, cooperation, and sense of adventure associated with traditional online role-playing games. Developed and published by Echo, the game combines open-world exploration, character progression, crafting, settlement construction, and multiplayer combat into an experience centered on player choice. Rather than following a strictly linear adventure, players are encouraged to establish their own objectives and participate in a persistent fantasy environment. Its greatest attraction is the possibility of creating a personal journey through exploration, cooperation, and community development. However, the ambitious scope also introduces challenges involving gameplay refinement, technical stability, and long-term player engagement.

Exploration forms an important part of the experience, with environments featuring forests, coastlines, settlements, caves, and other locations that encourage players to venture beyond familiar territory. Dynamic weather and changing lighting conditions contribute to the atmosphere, while activities such as fishing, sailing, and resource gathering provide alternatives to constant fighting. These elements help establish a world where everyday activities have practical significance. The freedom to explore without being continuously directed toward specific objectives is refreshing, although the enjoyment ultimately depends on the variety of discoveries and meaningful interactions available throughout the environment.

Character progression incorporates familiar MMORPG mechanics alongside opportunities for customization. Players can develop their chosen class, acquire equipment, improve abilities, and experiment with runes that modify their combat effectiveness. This approach encourages different character builds and potentially allows individuals to establish distinctive playstyles. The progression system provides incentives to participate in combat, explore dangerous locations, and obtain valuable resources. Nevertheless, maintaining balanced character development is essential, particularly when powerful equipment combinations could overshadow alternative strategies. Progression must also remain rewarding without becoming excessively dependent on repetitive grinding.

Combat emphasizes both individual preparation and cooperation. Dungeon encounters incorporate traditional party roles, including tanks, healers, and damage dealers, making teamwork important when confronting difficult enemies. Multiple dungeon difficulty settings offer increasingly demanding challenges and opportunities to acquire stronger equipment. This structure gives combat-focused players meaningful objectives beyond ordinary exploration. However, the effectiveness of these encounters depends on responsive controls, understandable enemy behavior, and interesting combat mechanics. Repeated battles can become monotonous when encounters rely too heavily on numerical difficulty rather than tactical variety.

One of the game's strongest concepts is its extensive construction and settlement system. Players can establish homes, furnish interiors, install crafting facilities, and modify portions of the surrounding terrain. Guilds can expand these possibilities by claiming territory and constructing shared settlements with defensive structures, walls, and gates. This gives community participation a tangible purpose, transforming collective resource gathering into visible improvements within the world. The ability to contribute toward a functioning settlement is particularly appealing for players who enjoy creative freedom and cooperative projects. However, construction systems require accessible interfaces and reliable management tools to prevent ambitious building projects from becoming unnecessarily frustrating.

Crafting and economic activities further support the sandbox philosophy. Gathering materials, farming, fishing, cooking, manufacturing equipment, and exchanging goods allow players to contribute without concentrating exclusively on combat. These interconnected occupations create opportunities for specialization and cooperation, potentially supporting a player-driven economy. Dedicated crafters can provide equipment to adventurers, while resource collectors and merchants help maintain the supply of essential materials. Unfortunately, such systems can lose their appeal if resource collection becomes repetitive or crafted items lack meaningful value. Their long-term success depends on balanced production requirements and sustained demand from an active community.

Competitive multiplayer introduces additional possibilities through PvP encounters, battlegrounds, and territorial conflicts. Guild settlements can become strategically important locations, encouraging players to coordinate defensive preparations and organize collective activities. This creates opportunities for memorable confrontations shaped by player decisions rather than predetermined scenarios. However, competitive balance remains a significant concern. Established groups can potentially dominate smaller communities, while inexperienced players may struggle against better-equipped opponents. Fair progression and accessible competitive opportunities are necessary to maintain a healthy multiplayer environment.

Visually, Ruin embraces a stylized three-dimensional medieval fantasy aesthetic. Its environments, structures, and character designs prioritize a recognizable fantasy atmosphere over photorealistic presentation. Weather effects and environmental lighting add character to exploration, while the relatively straightforward visual direction complements its independent development. Although the presentation has nostalgic charm, animation quality, interface clarity, and combat feedback remain important areas where refinement can significantly improve the experience. A visually modest MMORPG can still be engaging, provided its mechanics feel responsive and its environments remain interesting.

The free-to-play model makes the game accessible without requiring an initial purchase. Its stated monetization philosophy emphasizes cosmetic customization rather than selling direct combat advantages or accelerated progression. This is encouraging for an MMORPG involving competitive encounters and player-driven economic systems. Nevertheless, the game's Early Access nature means that players should anticipate incomplete features, balance adjustments, and occasional technical difficulties. Population size is another important consideration because dungeons, trading, guild activities, and PvP become considerably less engaging when there are insufficient active participants.

Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, Ruin currently has an Unknown verification status, meaning it has not been officially classified as Verified or Playable by Valve. Its Windows-oriented requirements and multiplayer interface introduce uncertainty regarding SteamOS compatibility, controller functionality, and handheld usability. Although Proton may potentially allow the game to operate, satisfactory performance and full functionality cannot be guaranteed. Players intending to experience it primarily on Steam Deck should therefore exercise caution.

Overall, Ruin presents an appealing vision of a community-driven fantasy MMORPG where exploration, combat, crafting, and settlement development contribute toward a larger shared experience. Its strongest qualities are its sandbox freedom, cooperative construction possibilities, and variety of activities beyond traditional dungeon grinding. However, uneven refinement, the challenges of maintaining an active multiplayer population, and the limitations associated with ongoing development prevent it from reaching its full potential. Players who appreciate experimental online worlds and gradual progression may find worthwhile entertainment here, particularly given its free-to-play accessibility. 

Rating: 6/10
